https://www.mediafax.ro/english/the-tria.text: The trial of Călin Georgescu and Horațiu Potra begins in the case regarding the attempted overthrow of the constitutional order Călin Georgescu is being tried for complicity in the attempted commission of actions against the constitutional order and the communication of false information, in continuous form, two material acts. Horațiu Potra is accused of attempting to commit actions against the constitutional order, failure to comply with the weapons and ammunition regime, failure to comply with the explosives regime, unlawful operations with pyrotechnic articles and public incitement. Alongside them, 20 other defendants are being tried, including Dorian Potra and Alexandru Potra, as well as several people whom prosecutors claim were part of the group mobilized by Horațiu Potra. The central accusation: the Ciolpani meeting after the annulment of the elections The case starts from the events of December 2024, immediately after the annulment of the presidential elections by the Constitutional Court. According to the indictment of the General Prosecutor’s Office, on December 7, 2024, between 10:51 and 12:01, Călin Georgescu allegedly met with Horațiu Potra at a riding center in Ciolpani, Ilfov County. Investigators claim that the meeting took place „under cover” and that the two discussed a plan for the following day. According to prosecutors’ allegations, Potra was going to mobilize people from his circle, including people with military training or specific operational capabilities, to participate in the protests scheduled in Bucharest on December 8, 2024. The plan, according to the Prosecutor’s Office, would have involved carrying out violent actions of a subversive nature, so that the initially peaceful demonstrations would be hijacked. Prosecutors state that the objective pursued was, by amplifying social tensions, „to change the constitutional order or to make it more difficult or prevent the exercise of state power.” What do prosecutors accuse Călin Georgescu of? In the case of Călin Georgescu, the Prosecutor’s Office claims that the organization of the meeting with Potra, the discussion of the plan and the subsequent actions contributed to strengthening the group’s determination to act. The investigators also invoked contacting the leader of a radical-nationalist organization and announcing Georgescu’s intention to send a „concrete action” message to supporters the following day. At the same time, prosecutors accuse the former presidential candidate of transmitting false information of an alarmist and potentially manipulative nature and of calling for the continuation of the vote, despite the cancellation of the election by the CCR. Potra’s group stopped on the way to Bucharest On the night of December 7 to 8, 2024, police stopped seven cars carrying Horațiu Potra and several of his relatives, who were traveling towards Bucharest. Weapons and objects such as knives and other edged weapons were found in the vehicles. According to information made public at the time, a pistol, knives, equipment and several sums of money were discovered in the car in which Potra was travelling. In subsequent searches of homes used by Potra and his associates, investigators announced the discovery of an arsenal that included grenades, firearms, ammunition and explosive materials. Prosecutors alleged that members of the group sought to infiltrate the protests that erupted after the annulment of the elections in order to cause violence and chaos. However, these allegations are yet to be analyzed and proven in court. The trial has finally passed the preliminary chamber Călin Georgescu, Horațiu Potra and the other defendants were sent to trial by the Prosecutor General’s Office’s indictment of September 15, 2025. On April 2, 2026, the Bucharest Court of Appeal found the legality of the indictment and the evidence and decided that the trial could begin. The decision was contested by both the defendants and the Public Ministry. The preliminary chamber procedure was prolonged after, at the High Court, one of the judges of the panel filed a request to abstain, and the debates had to be resumed in the new composition of the panel. On August 6, 2026, the High Court of Cassation and Justice definitively rejected the appeals and upheld the decision of the Bucharest Court of Appeal regarding the legality of the court referral. From that moment on, the case could enter the trial phase on the merits. Horațiu Potra recently escaped house arrest The trial begins less than a week after Horațiu Potra obtained a more lenient preventive measure. On September 3, the High Court admitted his appeal against house arrest and ordered his placement under judicial control for 60 days. The Bucharest Court of Appeal had previously upheld the house arrest on August 26, but this decision was changed by the supreme court. The first hearing on the merits is scheduled for Wednesday, September 9, at 1:30 p.m., at the Bucharest Court of Appeal. The judges will have to analyze the evidence presented by prosecutors, question the defendants and witnesses, and determine whether the charges in the indictment are proven. https://www.dw.com/en/storm-isaias-leave.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O7Qr Counties in Florida and Alabama had been under evacuation orders due to the storm Image: Joe Raedle/Getty Images/AFP Advertisement Storm Isaias has left four people dead as it moves across the southern United States , officials said Saturday. What's the latest on the storm? Two of the deaths were in Florida, while the other two were in Alabama. The storm originally made landfall on Friday evening as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida. It is the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season. Florida, Alabama and Georgia have all declared states of emergency due to the storm. According to PowerOutage.com, over 500,000 customers are without power in Florida and Alabama. The Florida Division of Emergency Management said approximately 5,000 Florida National Guard soldiers and airmen have been "activated to support impacted communities." A woman was killed in Florida after a tree fell on her home Image: Joe Raedle/Getty Images/AFP The storm brings heavy rainfall and powerfall winds, bringing the risks of flooding and tornadoes. It has ripped the roofs off buildings and downed trees in its wake. Storm moving into West Virginia The storm has weakened into a post-tropical cyclone and is moving over the southern US states of Tennessee and Kentucky into West Virginia, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC). In its latest update, the NHC warned of possible flash and urban flooding and said "landslides are possible across the Southern Appalachians." It also warned of wind gusts along with additional power outages and downed trees. In addition, swells from Isaias will continue to impact much of the Gulf coasts of the US, Mexico and western Cuba, and are "likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions." NHC said a couple of tornadoes are also possible across eastern Georgia and the Carolinas. Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon has hit Category 4 strength as it barrels towards Mexico's Pacific coast, where it is expected to make landfall on Sunday. The storm is expected to impact Puerto Vallarta, a popular destination for American tourists. Edited by: Dmytro Hubenko Don't let the algorithm hide the news. Photograph: Jim Wileman/The Guardian View image in fullscreen The Friends of Lower Field protesting against the sale of playing fields in Totnes, South Devon. Photograph: Jim Wileman/The Guardian Devon ‘We’re not playing games’: Parents launch playground protests to fight school field sell-off School looking to sell piece of open land beloved by people in Devon town to fund refurbishments Steven Morris Sat 17 Oct 2026 09.00 EDT Last modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 09.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google On Saturdays throughout autumn, residents of Totnes have met at a field on the banks of the River Dart to play ballgames, fly kites or simply sit on the grass and chat. But it hasn’t just been about having fun – this has been a “play protest” aimed at trying to save a beloved piece of open land in the historic Devon market town. The local comprehensive, King Edward VI Community College (KEVICC) , has been given the go-ahead by the UK government to sell the 1.5-hectare plot – Lower Field – and it is likely houses will be built on it. School leaders say they desperately need funds to revamp neglected buildings but campaigners claim the sell-off is an example of land that has been used by communities for decades being whisked away – a modern “enclosure” of public space. View image in fullscreen Anna Ali said there was ‘hidden impoverishment’ in the area. Photograph: Jim Wileman/The Guardian “It’s devastating,” said Becca Robinson, who uses the field for women’s and girls’ fitness classes. “I’m trying to get women and girls to be more active and to get outdoors. The great thing about the field is it’s an open space, so it feels safe. It really worries me that, if we lost it, fewer women and girls will exercise. “It’s also a spot people go just to do their own thing rather than take part in structured sport. You can just make an ad hoc decision to go and play a game or just to sit and read.” Earlier this year, the anti-poverty charity Trussell published research revealing almost half of UK residents (45%) had lost access to at least one community space – such as a park, social club, library or post office – since 2023. Danielle McIlven, who has been organising games of rounders on the field, attended the school and said Lower Field had been part of her life for years. “It’s about the unstructured play that can take place there. In the summer you see swarms of teenagers playing there or heading down to the river.” Anna Ali, the organiser of a women’s football “kickabout” and a member of the campaign group Friends of Lower Field , said the town had a reputation for being middle class and affluent. “But there is quite a lot of hidden impoverishment. Public green spaces are vital. I was speaking to a woman who brings her grandchildren here. They can’t afford to join sports clubs, so kicking a ball around on the field is a lifeline.” Lewis Winks, a leading member of the Right to Roam group, said Lower Field had been shared by the school and the wider Totnes community since it was gifted by the Elmhirst family, known for progressive farming, forestry and educational projects on the nearby Dartington Estate , about a century ago. View image in fullscreen Campaigner Lewis Winks said Lower Field had been shared by the school and community for about a century. Photograph: Jim Wileman/The Guardian A key issue the Friends group is digging into is the details of the Elmhirst gift – and whether it may have been legally given to the community or permanently protected for community use. Winks said: “Lower Field is a vital place for young people and families to play, exercise and spend time together. Losing it would undermine the town’s vitality and wellbeing.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion The Friends group wants Education South West, the trust the school is part of, to explore whether the field could be sold to the community. Winks said: “We are asking for a realistic window to raise the money. A community purchase could help fund improvements at KEVICC while safeguarding the field for its pupils and the wider community.” But it is a race against time. The land is expected to be put on the market in January, giving little time to raise funds. Campaigners also highlight that measures under the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 aimed at giving communities greater influence over the places and assets that matter to them are unlikely to come into force in time. “We’re falling through the gap regarding a right to buy,” Winks said. Matthew Shanks, chief executive of Education South West , said it understood how important the site was to the Totnes community and wanted to have an open and constructive conversation with people. He said money raised would support significant refurbishment and modernisation across the school estate, including improvements to buildings and facilities. Shanks said the school would retain playing fields which would remain available for public use. School principal Alan Salt said he understood the future of the field mattered hugely to the community. “We want to be open and transparent about what is proposed.” The trust and school have organised an open meeting to discuss the field. Salt argued that selling it made sound financial sense. There had been little capital investment in the school for six years and it had “temporary” classrooms more than half a century old. “So we’ve got a really acute set of challenges within a very difficult national context,” he said. “At the end of the day, we are a comprehensive school trying to get the best for the students in a really difficult national picture.” Explore more on these topics Devon Access to green space Schools School funding Land rights Communities Public lands news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Education Schools Teachers Universities Students
